Definition: of Hebrew origin (imperative of H1984 and H3050); praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation:--alleluiah.
BiblicalUsage: Four times, and all of them in one chapter, the song of heaven. After these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God. And again, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth; the word is Hebrew, praise ye Jah, carried whole into the Greek of Revelation.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for Alleluia carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is where it is sung, that heaven itself answers the fall of Babylon with praise, and the song does not stop.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
